clue.text: Play shots in various directions -— that's what batsmen are into

indicators.note: in places the stroke-playing word inside the string of compass points

parts.note: W, E and S are the compass points west, east and south
to hit is to play a shot with the bat

explanation.surface: A batsman flays the ball all round the ground, which is what he signed up for.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricketers traditionally play in white clothing, called their whites, so batsmen get into them before going out to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's traditional white flannels are known collectively by this name, and batsmen dress in them.

clue.text: Responses to roll-call shouted out? That's right

indicators.note: shouted out signals that the words are judged by how they sound when called

parts.note: at a roll-call each person answers 'here'; two such answers make 'here, here'

explanation.surface: Pupils call back at registration and someone confirms the tally is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here, here' (two answers at a roll-call) sounds like the cry of agreement heard in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry used in debates to show approval means the speaker is correct, an idiomatic endorsement.

clue.text: Express disapproval over early edition of Guardian

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval

indicators.note: an edition is a new version of a text, so the letters of early are put out in a new order

explanation.surface: A reader tuts at the first printing of the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places TUT above the rest in this down entry; ELARY is the rearrangement of EARLY. The Guardian newspaper is a red herring: the definition is the adjective 'of guardian'.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes a protecting spirit or patron, meaning relating to a protector or guardian.

clue.text: Naturally woken up, presumably, by axle all-night party

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Naturally woken up, presumably, by axle all-night party', has 'axle', which gives no letters of SLEEPOVER and fits no parse; likely an OCR garble, and the scan is unreadable
annotationWithheld.clue: Naturally woken up, presumably, by axle all-night party

clue.text: Hint, short and dull, where 1 ac say is situated

indicators.note: short means the hint word loses its last letter

parts.note: a clue is a hint
bland means dull, insipid

explanation.surface: A vague, tedious tip about where to find a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across, WHITES, is also White's, a famous gentlemen's club in St James's, London, the district of exclusive clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district of gentlemen's clubs is where White's, an example, stands.

clue.text: Secret fear, finally being caught in credit fraud

parts.note: a confidence is a secret told in trust

indicators.note: being caught in means the letter is trapped inside the credit word

parts.note: on tick means on credit, so tick is credit

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of fear

explanation.surface: Someone harbours a hidden dread of being exposed in a credit card scam.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle that wins a victim's trust before cheating them is a kind of fraud.

clue.text: Clear bishop ahead, took initiative and gave check gave check

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to rid is to clear
to take the initiative is to lead, so led

explanation.surface: A chess game: the bishop's path is opened, a player seizes the initiative and puts the king in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' puts the bishop's B in front of RID. The held text repeats 'gave check'; the definition is one copy. 'gave check' means restrained, as a rider reins in a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Reining in with a horse's headgear came to mean restraining or checking anything.

clue.text: Fiery man having retired has gone mad

parts.note: someone who has retired for the night has gone to bed, so is abed

indicators.note: mad signals the letters of gone are scrambled

explanation.surface: A hothead who has withdrawn from life has lost his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: NEGO is the rearrangement of GONE. In the Book of Daniel he was cast into the fiery furnace with Shadrach and Meshach.
explanation.definitionFit: This Biblical figure survived Nebuchadnezzar's fiery furnace, so is a man associated with fire.

clue.text: Translated widely, as poet

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet's work has been rendered into many languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil of this surname was an Anglo-Irish poet and Poet Laureate, so a poet.

clue.text: God formerly protected round church

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: protected means the word for formerly wraps around the ring shape

parts.note: then means at that former time
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A deity of old once guarded the parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because Rome's great temple to all the gods has long served as a Christian church.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Roman temple to all gods is now a consecrated church, Santa Maria ad Martyres.

clue.text: Line I followed, extremely uniform

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: A soldier recites his line and is told it was very uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinctive dress worn by servants or members of a guild is a uniform.

clue.text: Antony's success with broken hip shown by painter

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of hip are rearranged

parts.note: Filippo Lippi was a Florentine Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A painter's broken hip is shown alongside Mark Antony's triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: PHI is the rearrangement of HIP. Mark Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius at this battle in 42 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: The battle where Mark Antony defeated Caesar's assassins was his great military victory.

clue.text: Be about to offer money for mineral

indicators.note: about means the letters of be surround the lending word

parts.note: to lend is to offer money on loan

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of paying for a mineral specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc sulphide ore, also called sphalerite, is a mineral.

clue.text: Had second thoughts, having given in one's notice

definitions.meaning: written up in a critic's notice, that is assessed in a review

explanation.surface: An employee changed their mind after handing in their resignation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given in one's notice' looks like resigning from a job, but a notice is also a critic's write-up of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconsidered means had second thoughts; a critic's write-up is a review, so a show covered is this.

clue.text: Good to be upset about murder: it's wrong

indicators.note: about means the reversed pieces go round the killing word
upset in a down entry turns the pieces upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
to do in is slang for to murder

explanation.surface: Being good is turned upside down by a killing, and that is plainly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reads the good-and-live pair backwards in this down entry, giving EVILG; 'Good' looks like the opposite of the answer but only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked conduct is a wrong, a noun sense of the definition.

clue.text: Feel the heat, engaging a battle

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the heat word holds the a

parts.note: to fry is to feel intense heat

explanation.surface: A soldier sweats as he enters the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight or skirmish is a battle; one 'enters the fray'.

clue.text: Playwright's line saved by collector

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'Playwright is'

indicators.note: saved by means held safe inside the collector word

parts.note: a fetcher is one who fetches or collects

explanation.surface: A dramatist's line of dialogue is rescued by a collector of manuscripts.
explanation.definitionFit: John of this surname was a Jacobean playwright who collaborated with Beaumont and Shakespeare.

clue.text: Old woman stayed in, having got mean

indicators.note: stayed in means the woman's name sits inside the word for old

parts.note: aged means old
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An old woman stayed at home and became stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' looks like one phrase, but Old is AGED and woman is VERA; 'mean' is the statistical average, not stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: To calculate the arithmetic average of numbers is to find their mean.

clue.text: Loudly stir up emotional exchanges

indicators.note: loudly signals the word is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up

explanation.surface: Raising one's voice provokes heated arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy quarrels are heated, emotional exchanges, in the British sense rhyming with 'cows'.

clue.text: Irritated about English business having shrunk

indicators.note: about means the word for irritated goes round the other pieces

parts.note: riled means irritated
CO, company, is a business

explanation.surface: An Englishman is annoyed at a company that has downsized.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch back in fear or disgust is to shrink away.

clue.text: A know-all on the water, I take new The Times crew out

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A know-all on the water, I take new The Times crew out', contains the page header 'The Times' and its remaining words ('on', 'take', 'new', 'out') give no single honest parse; scan unreadable

clue.text: Team of doctors in attempt at perfection

definitions.meaning: a group of medical partners working together in one surgery
repeated exercise to improve, as in 'makes perfect'

explanation.surface: A group of GPs strives for flawless medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical partnership is called by this name, and so is rehearsal that 'makes perfect'.

clue.text: In worse physical condition, being comparatively mountainous?

definitions.meaning: more pale and sickly-looking, in British slang

explanation.surface: A hiker feels worse as the terrain grows more rugged.
explanation.walkthrough: Peaky is British slang for pale and unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of peaky means more unwell, and more full of peaks means more mountainous.

clue.text: Finally select pope's headdress

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of select

parts.note: Urban was the name of eight popes

explanation.surface: In the end a pope chooses his headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A long scarf wound round the head is a form of headdress.

clue.text: Sea flowing past bridge gap

parts.note: a tide is the sea flowing in or out
over means past, finished

explanation.surface: The sea rushes beyond a gap in a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To help through a difficult interval until something arrives is to bridge a gap.

clue.text: Dish witch offered to soldiers

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A witch serves a meal to the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish dish of offal cooked in a sheep's stomach is a meal for Burns Night.

clue.text: Left city in hands of fool, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in hands of means held between the outer parts of the fool word

parts.note: an idiot is a fool
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone says the city has been left to a fool, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's individual speech habits form their own personal manner of speaking.

clue.text: Right to have cried out, breaking fine Spode

indicators.note: breaking means the scrambled letters split the fine word open

parts.note: OK means fine

indicators.note: out signals the letters of cried are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone cries out for justice after smashing a fine piece of Spode china.
explanation.walkthrough: DERIC is the rearrangement of CRIED. Spode is not the porcelain: Roderick Spode is the would-be dictator in P G Wodehouse's Jeeves stories.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first name of Spode, the blustering fascist leader in P G Wodehouse's comic novels.

clue.text: Go and fetch device

parts.note: to gad is to go about idly
to get is to fetch

explanation.surface: Someone is sent off to bring back a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mechanical contrivance or tool is a device.
